overview: The Andean Wari developed an expansive society in Peru before the Inca. Provincial administration and roads accompanied a rich tradition of ceramics, textiles and personal ornaments.

items.text: An extensive road network connected the highland center with provincial establishments in more distant areas.
Provincial centers helped Wari authorities organize remote territories. Their distribution is evidence for political administration, not merely the spread of an art style.
Wari makers produced elaborate ceramics, sculpture and ornaments using inlays, gold and silver.
Surviving garments demonstrate a sophisticated textile tradition. Clothing was one of several important artistic media represented in Wari material culture.
Museum summaries use approximate periods beginning around 600 CE and ending around 1000 or 1100. Research must distinguish regional change from an empire-wide instant collapse.

sources.title: Cleveland Museum of Art: Wari, Lords of the Ancient Andes
